oliver: Heads up — noticed a 7-12% P99 tail latency increase in paginated-attn after the kernel routing change (PR #1234) rolled to canary. Any signals from infra? :eyes:
maya: Seen it in dashboards, looks concentrated on seq len ~1500-2048, batch 8-16.
rory: Which commit/sha? Can you paste the exact job id?
oliver: Commit 9f4b2a1, canary job run 2026-03-17T10:02Z id=canary-rl-78. Quick repro command I used:```bash
./bazel-bin/bench/attn_bench --seq=2048 --batch=8 --model=redwood-7b-paged
```
logs (truncated):```
[INFO] kernel_selected=flash_v2_variant_b seq=2048 batch=8 latency_ms=12.3
[WARN] fallback: kernel=blocked_paged_io latency_ms=34.9
```
zhen: Telemetry shows kernel routing probability for flash_v2_variant_b jumped from 18% -> 62% for seq>1024 after the change. Also KV page-fault rate up ~3x for the same jobs. Could be the kernel's memory working set interacting badly with the pagehouse allocator.
maya: Do we have a flamegraph or profile?
oliver: Yes, quick CPU/GPU split from perf trace (summarized):```
flash_attn_kernel::compute 42.1%
paged_kv_manager::page_in 18.7%
kernel_selector::choose 9.5%
memcopy_kv::async_copy 6.2%
other 23.5%
```
Looks like the chosen kernel increases page churn (more page-ins) which spikes latency at P99 even though median is similar.
rory: Interesting — so kernel selection favors a variant that trades a bit of compute for memory locality assumptions that don't hold under our pager. Could be exacerbated by batching heuristics too (bigger batches -> larger KV working set).
zhen: Bench numbers from my isolated runs: fused-flash v1: median 9.8ms P99 22.1ms; flash_v2_variant_b: median 10.4ms P99 33.7ms; when we force naive kernel route: median 12.0ms P99 24.0ms. So variant_b reduces median slightly but hurts tails.
oliver: Agreed. Quick mitigation options: 1) revert routing change 2) add heuristic to penalize kernels that cause extra page-ins (telemetry-driven) 3) pin kernel choice for seq>1024 to flash_v1 until we have allocator tweaks. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
maya: I can open a gated revert PR to roll canary back to old routing and add a feature-flag guard. I'll include a small telemetry patch to emit kernel->page-in rates per job.
rory: Also worth tuning batching heuristics: limit batch size for seq>1024 by default (or prefer chunked batching) — that reduces KV working set.
zhen: I'll run allocator microbench with the variant to see if fragmenting hot pages is the culprit. If allocator shows high slab churn we can try reserving a contiguous arena for KV pages as an experiment.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused for canary-rl-78 by automation due to P99 spike threshold breach. (job: canary-rl-78)
ci-bot: CI on revert PR would be gated behind perf tests. Unit tests ok.
oliver: Plan: @maya do revert + telemetry patch, @zhen run allocator microbench and post results in this thread, @rory draft batching tweak RFC. We'll reconvene after initial data. Thanks all :pray:
maya: on it, opening PR now. (reaction :thumbsup:)
